chunks: 5. Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qittan said: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qittan said: Bakr ibn Abd Allah ibn Hubayb said: Ali ibn Ziyad said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah said, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Abu Hayyan al-Taymi, on the authority of his father who was with Ali (peace be upon him) in the Battle of Siffin and onwards,

that While Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon him) was charging the battalions, Mu'awiyah came riding a horse towards him. Ali was on the horse of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) called al-Murtajiz. He had the spear of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) in his hand, and his own sword called Dhu al-Fiqar was hanging on his side. One of his companions said “Be careful, O Commander of the Faithful! Verily, we fear that this cursed man may kill you.” Consequently, he (peace be upon him) replied, Verily, if you had said that he is the most unfaithful and the most hard-hearted. He is the most wretched of the Kharijites due to his opposition to the rightly-guided Imams. Nonetheless, death is sufficient as a guardian. Everyone is protected by angels. They protect people fro falling into a well or a wall falling on them. They prevent people from other evils that may befall them. When the moment of death arrives, these angels guard people from what they are about to experience. I am the same. My death will come at the hands of the most wretched person of this Ummah, and my blood will color this and this. And he indicated his beard and head, saying it was “a well-know covenant and a true promise.” The tradition is detailed; we have extracted from it the required passage. I have transmitted all of it in the book Al-Dala'il wa al-Mu'jizat.

key_terms.الْقَاسِطِينَ: The Kharijites or those who deviate from justice
key_terms.ذُو الْفَقَارِ: Dhu al-Fiqar, the famous sword of Ali (AS)
key_terms.صِفِّينَ: Siffin, the location of the famous battle between Ali and Mu'awiyah
key_terms.مَلَائِكَةُ حَفَظَةٌ: Guardian angels who protect individuals until their death

ai.seo_question: What did Ali (AS) say about Mu'awiyah's ability to kill him during the Battle of Siffin?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq cites this narration to illustrate the Shia doctrine of *al-Ajal al-Mu'ajjal* (appointed time), emphasizing that divine protection prevents premature death until the destined moment arrives. The hadith highlights Ali’s confidence in his predestined martyrdom, linking the physical signs on his beard and head to the prophetic covenant of his death at the hands of Ibn Muljam, a key event in Shia eschatology.
